_doc: Personal quests from the House's own history (systems/houseQuests.js). Each is generated from real state — a townsperson's memory of the House (npcMemory), a town's memory, a lord's grievance (lordMemory), a lost heirloom — with objectives the engine checks and consequences that write back into memory, Prestige, renown, karma, standing and feuds. Text here is the template fallback; LlmProse retells it from the quest's facts when the model is on.

blood_price.title: The {kinCap} of {victim}
blood_price.hook: {holder} of {town} has not forgotten. {kinLine}{line} Word has reached your hall that the grudge is still nursed at their hearth.
blood_price.ask: Go to {town} and settle what lies between your House and {holder}: pay a blood price, ask forgiveness, or face them down.
blood_price.journal: {holder}, {kinPhrase}, still carries {deed}. It happened {years}. The matter waits in {town}.

pay.label: Pay the blood price
pay.desc: {price} gold into {holder}'s hands, and your head bowed.

plead.label: Ask forgiveness
plead.desc: No coin: only words. They may spit at your feet.

confront.label: Face them down
confront.desc: Tell them the matter is closed — or else.

old_debt.title: An Old Debt in {town}
old_debt.hook: A debt of your House is still counted in {town}. {kinLine}{line} {holder} says so to anyone who will listen.
old_debt.ask: Go to {town} and repay {holder} what your House owes, or deny the debt to their face.
old_debt.journal: {holder}, {kinPhrase}, still counts {deed} against your House. It happened {years}.

confront.label: Deny the debt
confront.desc: Your House owes nothing to the likes of them.

goods.need: the family has gone hungry since the last harvest
the winter came hard and the woodpile is gone
there is a death in the house and no light to keep the watch
there is to be a wedding and no wine to toast it

old_favour.title: What Is Owed Between Friends
old_favour.hook: {holder} of {town} sends word, calling on the old friendship. {kinLine}{line} Now {need}.
old_favour.ask: Bring {qty} {goodName} to {holder} in {town}, or send coin in their stead.
old_favour.journal: {holder}, {kinPhrase}, remembers {deed}. It happened {years}. They ask your House for help: {need}.

coin.label: Send coin instead
coin.desc: {price} gold, so they may buy it themselves.

refuse.label: Turn them away
refuse.desc: Old favours are paid; your House owes nothing.

threats: men are coming to collect a debt with cudgels
a band of toughs has sworn to burn the family out
an old feud of the street has turned to knives
protect.title: A Plea from {town}
protect.hook: A rider from {town} brings word: {holder} begs your House's protection. {kinLine}{line} Now {threat}.
protect.ask: Reach {town} within {days} days and stand by {holder} for {stay} days.
protect.journal: {holder}, {kinPhrase}, remembers {deed}, {years}, and has called on your House: {threat}.

heirloom.title: The Road to {heirloom}
heirloom.hook: {heirloom} of your House is spoken of in {place}. {holderLine}It has been gone {years}.
heirloom.ask: Go to {place} and bring {heirloom} home: buy it back, take it, ask for it, or search.
heirloom.journal: {heirloom} left the House {years} ({how}). The trail leads to {place}, where {keeper} has it.

lord_grievance.title: The Grievance of {realm}
lord_grievance.hook: {lord} of {realm} still holds {deed} against your House. {fromLine}The court of {realm} waits to see whether your House will mend it.
lord_grievance.ask: Go to {seat} and make amends to the crown of {realm}, or defy them.

defy.label: Defy the old grievance
defy.desc: What your forebears did is done. Say so.

town_amends.title: The Memory of {town}
town_amends.ask: Go to {town} and pay to rebuild and to remember, or leave the town to its bitterness.
town_amends.journal: {town} remembers {deed}, {years}. The town's folk speak of it still.

pay.label: Pay to rebuild
pay.desc: {price} gold into the town's coffers, for its walls and its widows.

words.holderLine: {holder} of {place} has sent word of it.

outcomes.settled: {holder} takes the {price} gold. The grudge is not gone, but it has been paid for.
outcomes.forgiven: {holder} hears you out, and at last gives a hand to shake. The old wrong is forgiven.
outcomes.spurned: {holder} turns their back on you. Your words were not enough.
outcomes.confronted: You face {holder} down. They say nothing more, but they will remember.
outcomes.repaid: {holder} counts the {price} gold twice and thanks you. The debt is cleared.
outcomes.denied: You deny the debt to {holder}'s face. Folk in {town} will hear of it.
outcomes.kept_faith: {holder} weeps to see the {goodName}. The old friendship holds.
outcomes.coin_sent: {holder} takes the {price} gold in place of the goods, with thanks.
outcomes.refused: You turn {holder} away. The old warmth between the families cools.
outcomes.protected: You stood by {holder} in {town} until the danger passed. No one came to harm.
outcomes.abandoned: No help came from your House. {holder} was hurt, and the family will not forget it.
outcomes.recovered: {heirloom} is back in the hands of the House.
outcomes.lord_mended: The crown of {realm} accepts the {price} gold. {lord} counts the old wrong mended.
outcomes.lord_defied: You defy the old grievance before the court of {realm}. {lord} will not forget it.
outcomes.town_rebuilt: The {price} gold goes to {town}'s walls and widows. The town will remember this too.
outcomes.lapsed: The matter with {holder} was left too long. It has hardened.
outcomes.lapsed_lord: No word came from your House. {lord} of {realm} takes the silence as an answer.
outcomes.lapsed_town: Your House never came. {town} keeps its memory as it was.
outcomes.gone: {holder} died before the matter was settled.

prose.hook: Write the news that reaches the ruler about this unfinished business of their House, in two or three sentences, as a steward reports it. Keep every name exactly.
prose.line: Write one or two spoken sentences in the voice of the person who holds this memory, said to the ruler's face. First person. Keep every name exactly.
prose.journal: Write the ruler's journal entry about this matter in two or three plain sentences. Keep every name and number exactly.
prose.epilogue: Write how this matter ended, as the House chronicle records it, in two or three sentences. Keep every name and number exactly.
